transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi doctor. I'm here because I've been struggling a lot with staying focused and paying attention to details lately. I keep making really careless mistakes, and it's starting to cause some real issues for me.
When did these attention and careless-mistake problems start, and were you having similar issues in childhood or school?

They've been particularly bad and causing real problems for about a year and a half now. However, I definitely remember struggling with these same attention issues and careless mistakes back in elementary school, well before I was 12.
Do you also often lose things, have trouble organizing tasks, or find it hard to follow through on assignments or chores?

Yes, I constantly lose important things like my keys, phone, or work documents. I also tend to avoid or really struggle to get through tasks that require a lot of mental focus, like chores or long assignments. I'm not quite sure about having trouble organizing, but those other two are definitely major issues for me.
Do you also often feel restless, fidget a lot, interrupt others, or act before thinking, or are your problems mainly with inattention?

My problems are definitely almost entirely with inattention rather than restlessness or impulsivity. I don't really fidget or interrupt people, but I constantly make careless mistakes, avoid mentally draining tasks, and lose important things.
Are these attention problems causing significant trouble in more than one area of your life, such as work, school, home responsibilities, or relationships?
To be honest, I'm not quite sure about that. I haven't really thought about it in that way, I just know it has been really frustrating to deal with lately.
Has this been causing clear problems at work or school, at home, or in your relationships, even if you have not thought about it that way before?

I'm still not entirely sure, as I haven't really thought about whether it has caused clear, major problems in those specific areas yet. Right now, I'm just mostly aware of how frustrating it is for me personally to deal with every day.
Can you give me one or two specific examples of how these attention problems have affected your work, school, home life, or relationships?

At work, I often put off writing big reports because they require so much mental focus, and when I finally do them, I make careless mistakes like entering the wrong numbers. At home, I constantly misplace my keys and wallet, which makes me late because I have to spend twenty minutes frantically searching for them.
Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

That diagnosis sounds incredibly accurate to me. I've been struggling with making careless mistakes, avoiding mentally draining tasks, and constantly losing my things for about a year and a half now. I also distinctly remember these same attention issues starting well before I turned 12.
Do you feel this diagnosis fits your symptoms and history?

I'm not entirely sure about the specific diagnosis itself, as I haven't really thought about it in medical terms before. I just know that these constant struggles with my focus and losing my things have been affecting me for a very long time.
Do you feel this diagnosis fits your symptoms and history?

To be honest, I'm not entirely sure since I'm not a doctor, but it does sound like it fits. I just know that these struggles with my focus and constantly losing my things have been affecting me for a really long time.

final_diagnosis.reason: Longstanding inattention since childhood with current symptoms of careless mistakes, difficulty sustaining attention on mentally demanding tasks, frequent losing of important items, and avoidance of sustained mental effort. Hyperactive/impulsive symptoms are absent, and the presentation is consistent with predominantly inattentive ADHD.
